messages.subject: possible bug in find_peaks()?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl,

I'm running into an interesting issue, and I'm not sure if it's a bug or I'm not understanding the scan1() function properly.

After a QTL scan, I'm looking for peaks with:
find_peaks(scan1,map = cross_combined$pmap,threshold = 4,drop = 1.5)

In this case, I'm getting the following peak:
lodindex lodcolumn chr      pos      lod    ci_lo    ci_hi
1        1    pheno1   3 92.17113 5.188023 28.43289 147.2141

As you can see, the confidence intervals are huge (~120 Mbp!). However, if I look at the plot of the scan, there are definitely LOD scores that are 1.5 LODs lower than the peak, around the peak (plot attached).

When I run the find_peaks function with peakdrop, this issue seems to go away:
find_peaks(scan1,map = cross_combined$pmap,threshold = 4,drop = 1.5,peakdrop=3)

 lodindex lodcolumn chr       pos      lod      ci_lo     ci_hi
1        1    pheno1   3  28.49419 4.157086   3.054919  29.17759
2        1    pheno1   3  92.17113 5.188023  81.163146  92.81123
3        1    pheno1   3 144.15531 4.117988 143.803494 159.92550

As you can see, the 2nd row shows a more acceptable 1.5 LOD confidence interval. Why wouldn't that show up when I didn't specify peakdrop? Wouldn't the 1.5 LOD interval be the same, regardless?

Thanks!

p.s. If I increase the peakdrop to 4, I get the same results as when I didn't include peakdrop.

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] possible bug in find_peaks()?
messages.body_plain:
This is as intended. If you don't provide peakdrop, then for drop=1.5 the interval will be from the first point where the LOD score is within 1.5 of the maximum to the last point where that is true. If peakdrop is defined as 3, it will be like that, but only for the region around the peak were the LOD score is within 3 of the maximum.

karl

messages.subject: R/qtl2 version 0.18
messages.body_plain:
I've released a new version of R/qtl2, version 0.18. Changes are listed below.

To upgrade:

    update.packages(repos="http://rqtl.org/qtl2cran")

Or do a fresh install:

    install.packages("qtl2", repos="http://rqtl.org/qtl2cran")

Also, the R/qtl2 paper is now published in Genetics. If you use R/qtl2, please cite:

Broman KW, Gatti DM, Simecek P, Furlotte NA, Prins P, Sen Ś, Yandell BS, Churchill GA (2019) R/qtl2: software for mapping quantitative trait loci with high-dimensional data and multi-parent populations. Genetics 211:495-502 doi:10.1534/genetics.118.301595 <https://doi.org/10.1534/genetics.118.301595>

karl

---

qtl2 0.18 (2019-02-08)
 <https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2/blob/master/NEWS.md#new-features>
New features

Added plot_lodpeaks() for scatterplot of LOD score vs position for inferred QTL from find_peaks() output.

Added new cross types "genril" and "genail", implemented to handle any number of founders; include the number of founders in the cross type, for example "genril38" or "genail38". The cross information has length 1 + number of founders, with first column being the number of generations and the remaining columns being non-negative integers that indicate the relative frequencies of the founders in the initial population (these will be scaled to sum to 1). "genril" assumes the progeny are inbred lines (recombinant inbred lines, RIL), while "genail" assumes the progeny have two random chromosomes (advanced intercross lines, AIL).

The internal function batch_vec() now made user-accessible, and takes an additional argument n_cores. This splits a vector into batches for use in parallel calculations.

The internal function cbind_expand() now made user-accessible. It's for combining matrices using row names to align the rows and expanding with missing values if there are rows in some matrices but not others.

In plot_peaks(), added lod_labels argument. If TRUE, include LOD scores as text labels in the figure.

Added function calc_het() for calculating estimated heterozygosities, by individual or by marker, from genotype probabilities derived by calc_genoprob().
 <https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2/blob/master/NEWS.md#minor-changes>
Minor changes

Small corrections to documentation.

Revise some tests due to change in Recla and DOex datasets at https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2data

Add tests of decomposed kinship matrix (from decomp_kinship()) with scan1().

rbind_scan1() and cbind_scan1() no longer give error if inputs don't all have matching attributes.

Change default gap between chromosomes in plot_scan1() (and related) to be 1% of the total genome length.
 <https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2/blob/master/NEWS.md#bug-fixes>
Bug fixes

Fixed bug in subset_kinship() that prevented scan1() from working with decomposed "loco" kinship matrices.

Fixed descriptions in help files for cbind.calc_genoprob() and rbind.calc_genoprob(), for column- and row-binding genotype probabilities objects (as output by calc_genoprob(). cbind() is for the same set of individuals but different chromosomes. rbind() is for the same set of markers and genotypes but different individuals. Made similar corrections for the related functions for sim_geno() and viterbi() output.

messages.subject: Rqtl2 input file issues

messages.subject: Permutation testing
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl,

Perhaps you could clarify something regarding permutation testing.
If I have 20,000 genes and I'd like to get a genome-wide LOD threshold via permutation, is it sufficient to permute 1 gene 1000 times, or should the entire set of genes be mapped for every permutation?

I was attempting the latter, but have found it to be computationally intractable.

-Basel
messages.body_snippet:

If I have 20,000 genes and I'd like to get a genome-wide LOD threshold via permutation, is it sufficient to permute 1 gene

messages.subject: Re: Permutation testing
messages.body_plain:
In principle, the significance thresholds for different genes may be different. In practice, their usually close to the same. But one advantage of transforming gene expression values to "normal quantiles" is that it they then all have the same distribution and so the same permutation threshold.

However, permuting a single gene will account for the multiple tests due to the scan across the genome, but not the search across the multiple genes. You could use an FDR approach there, e.g. using the qvalue package <https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/qvalue.html>. But there are some approaches for handling the search across the multiple genes that require permutations with all genes, jointly. See for example Neto et al. 2012 Quantile-based permutation thresholds for quantitative trait loci hotspots. Genetics 191:1355-65  doi: <https://doi.org/10.1534/genetics.112.139451>10.1534/genetics.112.139451

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Re: Permutation testing
messages.body_plain:
No, there are two separate issues: first, whether you can use the same significance threshold (from permutations with a single gene) for each of the 20k genes. And second, whether you need to account for the search across genes.

Regarding the first part, the answer is generally no, unless you've transformed the traits to all have the same marginal distribution, such as by transforming to normal quantiles. I don't mean quantile normalization but rather convert the gene expression values for a single gene to ranks and then find the corresponding normal quantiles. That is, you turn y1,...,yn  to R1,...,Rn where Ri is in {1, 2, ..., n}. Then take phi^-1 ( (Ri - 0.5)/n ) where phi^-1 is the inverse CDF of the normal distribution.

Regarding the second part, my point was that while some approaches to dealing with the multiple genes (such as FDR control with the qvalue package) can use just p-values calculated one at a time, other approaches (such as the Neto et al paper I cited) need permutation results with the traits analyzed jointly.

karl

messages.subject: Re: RIXs
messages.body_plain:
We don't have any code to analyze RIXs at present. And the mixed model would maybe need to be a bit fancier. Consider for example Zou et al (2005) Genetics doi:10.1534/genetics.104.035709 <https://doi.org/10.1534/genetics.104.035709>
You can analyze CCs and RIXs together, but I'm not sure I would want to do it. But I'm less trusting of the linear mixed model being sufficient to deal with the population structure.
I would prefer to analyze them separately and then overlay or combine the information.

karl

messages.subject: geneseek2qtl2 (myfread issue) for DO data
messages.body_plain:
I'm trying to process a set of 9 Geneseek GigaMuga and MegaMuga Final Reports in order to evaluate a Diversity Outbred sample in r/qtl2, using the geneseek2qtl2 function you've made available. Depending on which computer I'm using (probably to do with different versions of R and packages), I get warnings and/or errors using the internal myfread function. The issues have to do with whether myfread function can look past the header rows.

These Final Reports are large, not so simple to open in a text reader and edit by hand. I've looked them over in a large-file viewer, and all the headers are identical: 9 header rows with one or two columns of information per row.

Rather than worry about the way you intended these rows to be parsed, I'm thinking to just add the argument skip=9 inside myfread. I don't see anything inside geneseek2qtl2 that exploits information from the header, but I could be missing something. I wanted to confirm that here.

Thanks very much for any help.

David

messages.subject: Kinship matrix using BXD data
messages.body_plain:
I have a question on how best to use the kinship matrix given the following study design that employs BXD strains. We have two age time points  and two status (NonTg and Tg). We would like to model age and genotype as additive and interactive covariates (as and when appropriate). Since we are working with BXD strains we will, in essence, be replicating the strain genotypes so as to model these covariates. Is It valid to create a kinship matrix in this manner as well, where strains occur two or more times? Does this introduce a blocking structure that influences the mapping results?  Or, is it better to spit the data and model/map each slice separately with a kinship matrix where a strain occurs only once?

Thank you in advance for your help on this.
